refined_nucleus: A thin, porous, and negatively charged nanofiber mesh is integrated around the mechanical heart valve to mimic the natural glycocalyx and reduce platelet adhesion and coagulation activation, while also incorporating a shear-resistant material and a dynamic control system to adapt to changing blood flow conditions.
new_relationship: The nanofiber mesh's ability to reduce platelet adhesion and coagulation activation is directly correlated with its surface charge and porosity.
new_configuration: The nanofiber mesh is coated with a layer of negatively charged nanoparticles to enhance its ability to reduce platelet adhesion and coagulation activation.
new_control_rule: The dynamic control system adjusts the nanofiber mesh's surface charge and porosity in real-time to adapt to changing blood flow conditions.
refined_structure: The nanofiber mesh is co-located with the mechanical heart valve and is secured using a biocompatible adhesive. The negatively charged nanoparticles are evenly distributed across the nanofiber mesh.
refined_causal_chain: Thrombus formation on the mechanical heart valve
Nanofiber mesh reduces platelet adhesion and coagulation activation
Nanofiber mesh's surface charge and porosity are adjusted in real-time
Dynamic control system adapts to changing blood flow conditions
Reduced platelet adhesion and coagulation activation
Reduced risk of mechanical heart valve failure
addresses_attacks: The mechanism relies on the nanofiber mesh to mimic the natural glycocalyx, but there is no evidence that the mesh can effectively reduce platelet adhesion and coagulation activation under real-world conditions.

The transfer of the natural glycocalyx's properties to a mechanical heart valve is not justified, as the glycocalyx is a complex biological system that cannot be replicated by a simple nanofiber mesh.
The mechanism fails under high shear stress conditions, which are common in certain types of blood flow.
remaining_risks: The combination of a nanofiber mesh and a mechanical heart valve is not an obvious one, as it requires a deep understanding of both the biological and mechanical aspects of the system.
